ELI5: The difference between gcc and gcc-multilib, and why they are mutually exclusive.

The gcc-multilib supports multiple architectures and thus is required if, for example, you want to compile a 32bit binary on a 64bit system.

They are mutually exclusive because they are two versions of the same tool and it is just common consensus that packages be exclusive in that case.
Can I use the multilib version for everything, or will I need to change between them?

The features of "gcc" are a subset of the ones of "gcc-multilib", so, yes, the multilib version can definitely still compile for the same architecture as the local system.

So far I have not seen any downside to using the multilib one, except for the fact that having additional libraries around will use more hard-drive space.
